note: src/service/silence.c against build/test/t_fdspksil.  The claims: _status's escape byte, its code byte and its two-byte advance; silence_is_more_then's scale, its truncation and the direction of its comparison; and which fields silence_create writes.

label: _status writes the code first and the escape second
_status sets the length rather than advancing it
the silence scale is 8 per millisecond rather than 10
the silence comparison admits the boundary
the silence threshold rounds rather than truncating
silence_create stores its two arguments the other way round
silence_create leaves the run length at one

note: NOT here: removing silence_create's `if (s == 0) return 0` after the allocation.  The harness allocator never fails on request, so the arm is unreachable from any fixture and the mutant would read NOT CAUGHT while modelling nothing -- see t_fdspksil.c's header.  It is carried by the disassembly at 0xb03f8 (`xor %eax,%eax; test %edx,%edx; jne`), which is also what distinguishes silence_create from FIFO8_create, whose allocation is NOT checked.
